title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E510 treats the linearized bending of an upright column (axis length b, total weight M, elastic moment Ekk) whose cross-sections all carry the weight M dt/b. A horizontal force C dt/b is also distributed along the axis, and a horizontal force A acts at the end point A. The coordinate x runs along the undeflected axis from A, and y is the small lateral deflection.

The page finishes the moment balance about a running point Y = (x, y) of the deflected axis.

(i) Weight of the arc AY: the element at (t, u) carries vertical load M dt/b with lever arm y - u. Summed over the arc AU this gives (M/b)(yt - ∫u dt). Setting t = x, u = y gives (M/b)(xy - ∫y dx). Integrating by parts, d(xy) = x dy + y dx with xy = 0 at A, so this equals (M/b)∫_0^x x dy.

(ii) Balance (§20): the three moments are Ax (sinistrorsum), Cx²/(2b) (dextrorsum, from §18) and (M/b)∫x dy (sinistrorsum). Their net is set equal to the elastic moment Ekk/r:
  Ax + (M/b)∫x dy - Cx²/(2b) = Ekk/r.

(iii) The end reaction found earlier, A = C/2 + Mg/b, is inserted (g appears to be an end offset of the axis).

(iv) §21 linearization: for small y and constant dx, r = -dx²/ddy. This gives
  (C/2 + Mg/b)x - Cx²/(2b) + (M/b)∫x dy + Ekk y'' = 0.

(v) Dividing by M/b:
  (Cb/(2M) + g)x - Cx²/(2M) + ∫x dy + (Ebkk/M) y'' = 0.

Modern reading: the integro-differential equation of a heavy cantilever-type column under its own distributed axial weight plus a lateral distributed load. Differentiating once gives
  β y''' + x y' = Cx/M - (Cb/(2M) + g), with β = Ebkk/M.
So p = y' satisfies the inhomogeneous Airy equation β p'' + x p = const + linear term. This is the Greenhill heavy-column problem (Bessel functions of order ±1/3). On the next page Euler says it can only be solved by infinite series, and §22 there fixes the boundary conditions y(0) = 0, y ≈ αx near A, and the integral vanishing at x = 0.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The by-parts step xy - ∫y dx = ∫x dy is exact because xy vanishes at A.
The sign conventions (r = -dx²/ddy, directions sinistrorsum/dextrorsum) are consistent.
Minor dimensional looseness only appears on the next page (M = b³ via 'amplitudo' bb), not here.

ideas.what: Moment of the distributed self-weight about a running point of the deflected axis written as (M/b)∫x dy via integration by parts
ideas.modern_name: Bending moment from distributed axial load in the linearized heavy-column (Euler–Bernoulli) model
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1778 column papers); later Greenhill (1881) for the closed form

ideas.what: Linearized curvature r = -dx²/ddy and reduction to an integro-differential equation whose derivative is of Airy type
ideas.modern_name: Heavy column equation EI y''' + q x y' = f(x); Airy/Bessel order-1/3 solutions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (series form); Greenhill 1881 (Bessel functions); Airy 1838 (for the function)
ideas.where_published: E510 itself; discussed by Truesdell, The Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Superposed lateral distributed load C dt/b and end force A combined with self-weight
ideas.modern_name: Beam-column under combined axial self-weight and transverse load

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine moment-balance derivation in a well-studied Euler paper on heavy columns, whose history (Euler 1778, Greenhill 1881) Truesdell surveyed. The Airy-type structure is implicit but already recognized in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Transcription matches the image. The only differences are minor typographic ones (e.g. the image prints the 1/2 in front of C as a small fraction, ½C).
